steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: distinguish three location records
steps.detail: A browsing location helps select nearby food; a saved address is an owned customer record; an order address is the historical destination agreed for that order. They may initially contain similar coordinates, but they have different owners and lifetimes. Read the User-Chef README and CustomerAddressRequestValidationTest before editing address fields. The test suite covers required recipient, area and postal information, latitude presence, longitude bounds and temporary missing-district compatibility. That compatibility is evidence of a rolling contract, not permission to delete every validation rule. Follow address selection through the customer client, the User-Chef API and the snapshot consumed by checkout. Do not label the customer's current browsing map pin as the historical delivery destination. A UUID identifies a record; it does not prove that the caller owns it.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: edited and unavailable addresses
steps.detail: Use a synthetic customer with two saved addresses and an existing order. Change the current saved address in a disposable fixture and explain why the existing order must retain its original destination. Test a deleted or inactive saved record separately from a malformed address request. A frontend validation message cannot replace backend ownership and shape checks. When investigating, capture the address identifier, field presence and sanitized validation code rather than the full home address or telephone number. Specify which layer should reject an invalid coordinate before a paid checkout is attempted. Do not invent delivery-radius rules or postcode coverage from coordinate validity: a geometrically valid point may still be unserviceable.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: prove the address contract before extending it
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -ntp -f services/user-chef-service/pom.xml -Dtest=CustomerAddressRequestValidationTest test from a local clone. Read each fixture and record expected behavior for complete data, missing recipient, missing area, missing postal code, absent latitude, out-of-range longitude and omitted district. In a training branch add a boundary fixture rather than relaxing the validator. Produce a field map with source, type, nullability, owner and downstream snapshot requirement. For any proposed optional address field, explain how an older mobile client and an older order record behave when it is absent. Do not call a production geocoder, copy a real home address into Git, or change active records.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a seven-case validation matrix, one new local boundary test, and a comparison showing why an address edit is not an order-history edit. Mark delivery coverage as product/provider evidence, not an inference from these validation tests.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: follow an application and its evidence
steps.detail: AdminDirectoryController routes protected case reads through /api/v1/admin/directory. getChefCase in AdminDirectoryService reads chef_application, related chef_kyc_document records and admin_chef_decision_audit. Keep these different record types separate in your explanation: an application expresses a request, a document is submitted evidence, and an administrator decision is an audited action. The directory view is not itself a kitchen activation engine. Trace the identity identifier into the application lookup and the application identifier into its documents. Identify the operational reason required by the API and the correlation identifier returned with the response. Never equate possession of a document with a legal compliance conclusion or assume that a UI status automatically creates a live Catalog kitchen.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: ambiguous statuses and sensitive evidence
steps.detail: Build a scenario where an application exists but a downstream kitchen is not yet visible. Check application state, decision evidence, downstream propagation and Catalog state independently. An empty document list may mean no documents, denied access or an upstream error; those states must not collapse into an approved status. Do not paste identity documents, bank details, signed document URLs or private addresses into course examples. When requirements mention compliance, record the approved functional-spec section and authorized reviewer decision. Engineering can enforce the accepted workflow and audit it; it must not choose an FSSAI interpretation, override the reviewer or manufacture a legal status.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: reconstruct a synthetic onboarding case
steps.detail: Open AdminDirectoryController.java and AdminDirectoryService.java in the source viewer. Draw the application-to-document-to-decision relationships, then annotate which fields are identifiers, statuses, timestamps and private evidence. Run mvn -B -ntp -f services/user-chef-service/pom.xml -Dtest=AdminDirectoryServiceTest test. Verify that authorization and operational-reason rejection happen before database access. Create a tabletop case with an existing application, zero documents and no decision, then a second with a decision but delayed downstream visibility. Write expected UI states and the next diagnostic read for each. This is a mock case reconstruction, not permission to approve a chef or fetch real KYC records.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a synthetic case timeline, evidence relationships and a distinction between application approval, document review and operational kitchen visibility. Every claimed transition must have an identified owner rather than a guessed status mapping.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: trace an audited directory request
steps.detail: Read AdminDirectoryController.search, customerCase and chefCase. Search is a POST to /search; individual cases are GET requests under /customers/{identityId} and /chefs/{identityId}. All require X-Admin-Reason in the reviewed controller. The noStore helper attaches Cache-Control: no-store and X-Correlation-ID using the correlation value returned by the service. Follow the principal supplied by @AuthenticationPrincipal into the service checks, then the bounded search classification and parameterized queries. A path identity selects the subject of an authorized investigation; it is not the identity of the administrator performing it. Explain both identities explicitly in your trace. This separation is the foundation of auditability when one authorized user investigates another person's records.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: search must remain bounded
steps.detail: A directory search can expose far more personal information than a single owned-profile lookup. Check allowed roles, reason length, query validation, result bounds and the returned DTO before making it more flexible. Parameterized SQL is different from concatenating a user's search string into SQL. Do not widen a bounded lookup into unrestricted bulk export merely to support a search box. Inspect how missing records differ from bad requests and how correlation information is generated. A new response adapter must preserve the canonical correlation identifier rather than replacing it with a different random value and causing an investigation mismatch.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: map inputs to outputs with no live queries
steps.detail: Create a worksheet for each directory operation containing request method/path, principal source, subject ID, required reason, service method, queried record types, response DTO and no-store/correlation behavior. Use synthetic strings in all samples. Run AdminDirectoryServiceTest and inspect rejectsNonAdminBeforeTouchingDatabase, rejectsMissingOperationalReasonBeforeTouchingDatabase and rejectsUnboundedFreeTextBeforeTouchingDatabase. Add one local test for a nearby invalid input and prove that the database dependency is not invoked. Review the client parser separately: TypeScript types do not validate an HTTP response at runtime. Explain how a malformed response becomes a visible diagnostic error rather than an empty customer case.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: three complete request maps and a negative-input test that checks absence of database access. A reviewer should be able to distinguish administrator, investigation subject and correlation identifiers throughout the flow.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: build a derived case summary safely
steps.detail: Training-only feature brief: add a read-only count of active saved addresses to an already authorized synthetic customer-case view. Do not add a new customer search mode, change onboarding decisions or create a production feature. Start in AdminDirectoryService.getCustomerCase and the corresponding DTO in AdminDirectoryDtos. Determine whether the authorized case already contains the necessary active-address facts. Prefer a derived value over a new stored counter that could drift. Keep the same subject scope, administrator guard, reason and audit behavior. Then identify the exact web adapter and component using that case response before writing client code. A vertical slice includes contract, service, tests, adapter and rendering; it is not just a label on a page.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: privacy and compatibility are requirements
steps.detail: Define zero, one and several active-address fixtures plus an unauthorized caller. Clarify that inactive rows must not inflate the displayed count when the existing case contract only returns active addresses. Do not introduce an unscoped SELECT count(*) across customers. New optional response fields should be tolerated by older clients; the new client must have explicit behavior if an older backend omits the count. Decide whether the value is a convenience derived locally from the already authorized DTO or a server-owned contract addition, and justify the choice. Do not guess which other profile fields should become mandatory in order to make the exercise interesting.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: implement the complete training change
steps.detail: In a local branch named training/customer-case-summary, write the acceptance tests first. Add the derived response value at the appropriate existing boundary and a runtime client parser test. Render zero, loading, ready, denied and temporarily unavailable states without exposing address text in a compact summary. Run the focused User-Chef tests and the relevant web tests/typecheck. Inspect the generated JSON to verify that no extra personal fields leaked as a side effect. Deliver a file-by-file change list, synthetic before/after response, tests and backward-compatibility note. The source owner should be able to reject unnecessary schema changes or a second Node business implementation from the plan alone.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: the working local slice, an owner-scoping test, a no-extra-PII response assertion and an explanation of why no new database counter was needed. Publishing this training solution to production requires a separate reviewed feature request.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: test lifecycle and contract together
steps.detail: Profile and onboarding changes cross identity, persistence, administrative review and client boundaries. Choose tests by risk: request validation catches malformed addresses, service tests check denied investigations before data access, and client contract tests catch response-shape drift. A migration, when genuinely needed, must account for existing rows and deployed older clients. Never rewrite an applied migration to make a fresh database look cleaner. The rollback question is whether the previous application can still read records created by the new application. Retain an approved correction/audit path for existing records instead of relying on manual SQL updates when a profile is inconsistent.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: recover at the failed boundary
steps.detail: When a customer-case screen is broken but User-Chef returns a valid authorized response, investigate the BFF/parser/UI instead of restarting payment or delivery. When an onboarding decision is valid but propagation is delayed, reconcile the specific downstream work and preserve the decision audit. When a source record is wrong, collect the original state, expected state and authorized correction reason without overwriting evidence. Do not turn a downstream outage into a new chef approval or delete documents to force a retry. Treat secret rotation, scaling and deployment of unrelated services as separate changes, not default troubleshooting actions.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: produce a release and recovery evidence set
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -ntp -f services/user-chef-service/pom.xml -Dtest=CustomerAddressRequestValidationTest,AdminDirectoryServiceTest test against local mocks. Inventory any additional database-backed suite before enabling its environment variables. Prepare expected/actual/pass-fail rows for validation, denied role, required reason, bounded search, canonical correlation, no-store headers, subject isolation and old-client compatibility. Write a mock deployment record with an immutable source/image pair, prior healthy revision and a one-replica preservation check; leave unobserved live fields explicitly pending. Finish with a tabletop rollback of the training case-summary field and show that neither customer records nor other service configurations need to be deleted.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: an auditable change packet with test scope and limitations, a narrow rollback, and no real personal information. Explain which evidence would still be required for a live onboarding or address-flow acceptance.
